item.title: Xi arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO summit, state visit
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
Xi arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO summit, state visit Updated: August 30, 2026 15:38Xinhua BISHKEK, Aug. 30 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping landed in Bishkek on Sunday for the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 and a state visit to Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Xi kicks off state visit to Kyrgyzstan, hailing 'golden period' of cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
BISHKEK, Aug. 30 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping landed in Bishkek on Sunday for a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026. The China-Kyrgyzstan cooperation has ushered in a "golden period" of rapid development, Xi said in a written speech delivered upon his arrival. TIME-HONORED FRIENDSHIP Noting that China and Kyrgyzstan share a time-honored traditional friendship, Xi said that the majestic Tianshan Mountains stand as witnesses to the millennia of friendly exchanges between their peoples. Over the 34 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the China-Kyrgyzstan relationship has withstood the test of a changing international landscape, maintained sound and stable development throughout, and reached the high level of a comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, Xi said. In recent years, bilateral trade volume and people-to-people exchanges have reached new highs, Xi said, noting that major projects including the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway have been successfully implemented, and the tangible results of mutually beneficial cooperation have broadly benefited the two peoples. Xi said that during the visit he will have in-depth exchanges of views with Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov on China-Kyrgyzstan relations, cooperation in various fields between the two countries, and international and regional issues of common concern, and draw a new blueprint for building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future. "I look forward to attending the SCO Bishkek Summit, working with all parties to revisit the 25-year development experience of the SCO, jointly discuss cooperation plans, create the future of the organization, and promote the continuous new development of the SCO," Xi said. HIGH-QUALITY DEVELOPMENT OF TIES Ahead of his state visit to Kyrgyzstan and attendance at the SCO summit, Xi on Friday published a signed article titled "Jointly Opening up New Prospects for the High-Quality Development of China-Kyrgyzstan Relations" in the Slovo Kyrgyzstana and the Kabar National News Agency. Noting that it will be his third visit to this beautiful land, Xi said he looks forward to working with President Japarov to map out a new blueprint for China-Kyrgyzstan relations and make new progress in building an SCO community with a shared future. Describing the two countries' relations as a "golden model" of good-neighborly friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation, Sheradil Baktygulov, director of the Kyrgyz Institute of World Politics in Bishkek, said high-level exchanges have provided clear strategic guidance for the deepening of bilateral relations and closer coordination between the two countries in international affairs. In the signed article, Xi said that China and Kyrgyzstan are good neighbors sharing weal and woe, good partners with a shared future, and good friends who help each other succeed. "When a neighboring country is genuinely happy about your success, that sincerity is truly precious. It reflects President Xi's respect for Kyrgyzstan, its people and the development path they have chosen," said former Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Alikbek Jekshenkulov. Noting the improved understanding between the two peoples, Jekshenkulov said such mutual understanding has kept bilateral friendship enduring and vibrant, allowing it to be passed down from generation to generation. In February 2025, Xi and Japarov reached important common understandings on further deepening the comprehensive strategic partnership for the new era and building a China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future defined by good-neighborliness, friendship and shared prosperity. The decision opened a new chapter of bilateral relations. In the signed article, Xi said China and Kyrgyzstan have complementary economies and immense cooperation potential. Despite sluggish global growth, the two countries' business cooperation has continued to make steady progress. Tolonbek Abdyrov, professor of economics and vice rector of the International Higher School of Medicine in Kyrgyzstan, said the two countries enjoy enormous potential for cooperation. "Chinese investment has not only enabled Kyrgyzstan to implement a number of major infrastructure, energy and industrial projects, but has also created opportunities to accelerate the country's modernization." Noting that Xi's signed article provides strong guidance for the sustainable development of bilateral cooperation, Kyrgyz economist Iskender Sharsheev said: "The two sides enjoy enormous potential for cooperation in such fields as the digital economy, green energy, and artificial intelligence." In the article, Xi also called on the two sides to solidify good-neighborliness and friendship, pursue mutual benefit and win-win results, carry forward the traditional friendship, and practice multilateralism. Xi said China is ready to work with Kyrgyzstan to steadily advance their multifaceted cooperation, channel the streams of the two peoples' goodwill into the river of the two nations' friendship, and jointly open up new prospects for the high-quality development of China-Kyrgyzstan relations. On the SCO summit, Xi said China is convinced that with the concerted efforts of all sides, this year's SCO summit will be a crowning success and provide fresh impetus for carrying forward the Shanghai Spirit and building an SCO community with a shared future. Professor Almazbek Akmataliev, former rector of the Academy of Public Administration under the President of Kyrgyzstan, said in today's international environment, Xi's call for further carrying forward the Shanghai Spirit has become increasingly relevant. HOPES FOR GREATER COOPERATION People across Kyrgyzstan see Xi's visit as an important opportunity to deepen political trust, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, and boost people-to-people ties, which will inject new impetus into bilateral relations. "We are witnessing one of the most meaningful and fruitful periods in the history of Kyrgyz-Chinese relations," said Jekshenkulov. Xi's visit will represent not only another milestone, but also an opportunity to elevate bilateral ties to a new level, he said. Kanaiym Baktygulova, former Kyrgyz ambassador to China, has witnessed the development of bilateral ties at close range. She said the political wisdom and strategic vision of the two leaders have provided a solid foundation for the growth of bilateral relations and charted a clear course for future cooperation. Baktygulova said she expected Xi to put forward new proposals for deepening mutual political trust and expanding win-win cooperation. Noting that Kyrgyzstan is implementing its National Development Program until 2030 and China is advancing the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), Elkinbek Ashirbaev, governor of Kyrgyzstan's Chui region, voiced his hope that Xi's visit will help bring the two countries' development strategies into closer alignment. For Kyrgyz economist Abdyrov, China's experience in infrastructure, industrial modernization and the clean energy industry is particularly relevant to his country's development needs. Abdyrov also sees useful lessons in China's approach to long-term development. Strategic planning and consistent industrial policies can offer insights into Kyrgyzstan's pursuit of sustainable growth, he said, adding that the visit could encourage further exchanges on governance. In recent years, people-to-people and cultural exchanges between China and Kyrgyzstan have continued to deepen and yield tangible results. Zhyldyz Bakashova, director of the State Book Chamber, said she expects Xi's visit to promote further cooperation in book publishing and translation, helping readers in both countries better understand each other's cultures. The two countries are also working together to study and protect cultural heritage through the China-Kyrgyzstan Belt and Road Joint Laboratory on Cultural Heritage Conservation. "By studying and protecting cultural heritage together, we have gained a deeper understanding of the histories of both countries," said Aisin Duishanalieva, the laboratory's Kyrgyz director, expecting the leaders' meeting to offer further support to that collaboration. At a time of heightened global uncertainty, Kyrgyz-China collaboration in the United Nations, the SCO and other multilateral forums has become increasingly valuable, said Baktygulov, highlighting China's support for Kyrgyzstan's successful election in June as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council. Baktygulov said he expects the visit to strengthen bilateral communication and coordination on regional and global affairs, and promote joint efforts to maintain regional stability, enhance dialogue and seek solutions to hotspot issues.

item.title: China sees 7 pct rise in newly established foreign-invested enterprises in H1
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-29
BEIJING, Aug. 29 -- China saw 35,000 newly established foreign-invested enterprises in the first half of 2026, up 7 percent year on year, the State Administration for Market Regulation said Saturday. By region, both major exporting provinces and border regions recorded growth in newly established foreign-invested enterprises, according to the administration. Among the major exporting provinces, the number of newly established foreign-invested enterprises rose 38.6 percent year on year in Hainan, 15.2 percent in Shandong, 8.1 percent in Guangdong and 6.8 percent in Jiangsu. With the launch of island-wide special customs operations at the Hainan Free Trade Port on Dec. 18, 2025, Hainan has introduced a series of opening-up policies aimed at fostering a foreign investor-friendly business environment. By sector, the consumer market emerged as a new area attracting foreign investment. The number of newly established foreign-invested enterprises in health and social work increased 27.1 percent year on year, while those in wholesale and retail rose 11.9 percent and those in accommodation and catering grew 11.7 percent. Separate data from the Ministry of Commerce showed that almost 4,800 foreign-funded enterprises made additional investments in China in the first half of this year, while foreign direct investment in high-tech industries surged 33.2 percent year on year. In June, China's commerce ministry, alongside other government departments, released an action plan to stabilize and optimize foreign investment utilization, detailing 15 measures. The plan prioritizes wider market access in the services sector and also calls for efforts to promote the "Invest China" initiative and ensure foreign-funded enterprises' concerns over equal participation in government procurement and fair access to business operations are fully addressed.

item.title: China's new economic growth drivers index rises 12.5 pct in 2025
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 27 -- China's new economic growth drivers index rose 12.5 percent in 2025, with the transformation and upgrading index and the innovation driven index together accounting for nearly two-thirds of the increase, official data showed Thursday. The index reached 153, with 2022 set as the base year of 100, according to the Institute of Statistical Sciences of the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS). All four sub-indexes increased from a year earlier. The transformation and upgrading index rose 22.7 percent, the fastest among the four, and contributed 34.1 percent to overall index growth. The innovation-driven index increased 12.9 percent and contributed another 31.4 percent, bringing their combined contribution to 65.5 percent. That marked a shift from 2024, when the network economy was the largest contributor to index growth and transformation and upgrading accounted for 16.7 percent of the increase. Lyu Haiqi, head of the NBS institute, said in an analysis accompanying the index release that China's new growth drivers continued to grow in strength in 2025, with innovation playing an increasingly prominent leading role and transformation and upgrading gathering pace. He said the developments helped China make new progress in high-quality economic development. On transformation and upgrading, Lyu noted that the value added of high-tech manufacturing rose 9.4 percent in 2025, 3.5 percentage points faster than that of major industrial enterprises as a whole. The share of the value added of high-tech manufacturing in the total value added of major industrial enterprises rose to 17.1 percent. Lyu cited continued efforts to advance the digital transformation of manufacturing, the "AI Plus" initiative, technological upgrading and intelligent manufacturing, alongside the green transformation of key industries. He also pointed to faster growth in strategic emerging industries and continued development of future industries. Exports of electric vehicles, photovoltaic products and lithium batteries -- often referred to as China's "new three" -- approached 1.3 trillion yuan (191.6 billion U.S. dollars) in 2025, up 27.1 percent, he noted. Lyu also pointed to increased innovation input. China's expenditure on research and development reached 3.9 trillion yuan in 2025, up 8.1 percent and equivalent to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product. Spending on basic research and the value of technology contracts both recorded double-digit growth. The network economy index rose 10.8 percent. Lyu pointed to the continued expansion of digital infrastructure and the development of new forms of consumption and trade, including instant retail, livestreaming e-commerce and cross-border e-commerce. The economic vitality index increased 4.8 percent. Lyu cited continued reform efforts, including measures to build a unified national market, a new version of the negative list for market access and efforts to advance market-oriented allocation of production factors. The index measures developments in 2025. Separate data for 2026 showed high-tech manufacturing continuing to post faster value-added growth than major industrial enterprises as a whole. In the first seven months, the value added of high-tech manufacturing rose 13.8 percent year on year, compared with a 5.3-percent increase in the total value added of major industrial enterprises, NBS data showed earlier this month. The NBS said new growth drivers witnessed robust development and the economic structure continued to improve. Separate industrial profit data released Thursday showed profits in high-tech manufacturing growing faster than overall industrial profits. Profits of major industrial enterprises rose 17.6 percent year on year in the first seven months, while profits of high-tech manufacturers rose 50.1 percent.

item.title: China sets 2030 goals for logistics network development
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
BEIJING, Aug. 28 -- China has set goals to advance the development of the country's logistics network by 2030, aiming to improve connectivity and better support the real economy, according to a plan released by the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and the Ministry of Transport. By 2030, China expects to make notable progress in developing its logistics network with closer coordination between logistics hubs and industries, enhanced internal and external connectivity, greener and smarter facilities and equipment, and greater interoperability of rules and information, according to the plan. The plan aims to help effectively reduce logistics costs across society, bringing total social logistics costs to 13.1 percent of GDP by 2030, down 0.8 percentage points from the end of 2025. This will help improve the efficiency and performance of the real economy and support smoother economic circulation and high-quality development, it said. The plan outlines 17 key tasks in seven areas, including advancing the development and connectivity of logistics hubs, enhancing the capacity of logistics corridors, addressing shortcomings in urban and rural logistics facilities, and promoting the digitalization, smart development and green transformation of logistics facilities and equipment. The logistics network is one of the six networks prioritized during China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), alongside water networks, new-type power grids, computing power networks, next-generation communication networks and urban underground pipeline networks. The NDRC has described the six networks as an integrated whole featuring deep interconnection, mutual empowerment and coordinated support. Investment in the six networks and key areas is preliminarily estimated to exceed 7 trillion yuan (about 1.03 trillion U.S. dollars) this year.

item.title: Chinese premier urges all-out rescue, emergency response efforts after Gyirong mudslide
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-28
GYIRONG, Xizang, Aug. 28 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has called for all-out rescue and emergency response efforts following a mudslide that struck the Gyirong border port in Gyirong County of southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. Entrusted by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, traveled to Gyirong County on Thursday to guide rescue and emergency response efforts after the disaster. Five people have been confirmed dead and 558 others are missing after the mudslide hit the border port on Wednesday morning, according to regional authorities. Xi, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made instructions on disaster relief and emergency response operations after the mudslide occurred on Wednesday. Li stressed the importance of implementing the instructions, calling for efforts to put the people and their lives above all else and to spare no effort in carrying out rescue and emergency response work. After arriving at the Xigaze airport, Li proceeded directly to the disaster-hit area in Gyirong, where he inspected the damage and met with rescue workers. Li said rescue plans should be formulated in a scientific manner and every possible effort be made to search for those who are still missing. As long as there is a glimmer of hope, every effort should be made, he said. He also called for swift repairs to damaged infrastructure, including roads, communications and power facilities, to restore access for rescue operations as soon as possible. Expressing appreciation to personnel working on the front lines of the rescue effort, Li later visited temporary shelters for affected residents and conveyed Xi's concern and care to them. Li stressed the need to continue dispatching and transporting disaster-relief supplies and ensure the basic living needs of evacuated and relocated residents. At the front-line command center for the Gyirong mudslide disaster response, Li called for strengthening coordination of rescue personnel and equipment, enhancing unified on-site command, and further efforts to fully ascertain the situation of those still missing. He stressed the need to carry out rescue operations in an orderly and effective manner. It is necessary to strengthen monitoring, forecasting and early warning of weather, hydrological and geological conditions in affected and surrounding areas, as well as take solid epidemic prevention and disinfection measures to guard against secondary disasters, he noted. He urged authorities to release information on the disaster and rescue operations in an open and transparent manner. Li also stressed the need to strengthen foreign-related emergency response, communication and coordination, and work with relevant foreign parties to verify the status of missing persons and well handle follow-up matters. Noting that China is still in the midst of flood season and faces a severe and complex situation regarding flood control and typhoon prevention, Li called for maintaining preparedness for extreme and worst-case scenarios. He urged authorities to remain highly vigilant, intensify inspections and risk-removal efforts in key areas and vulnerable locations, and take solid measures against various natural disasters to safeguard people's lives and property and maintain overall social stability.

item.title: China tightens accountability for officials regarding ecological, environmental damage
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- Chinese officials found responsible for serious ecological and environmental damage will be held accountable for life, even if they have since left their posts, according to a recently released policy document. Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, the document outlines the cases that can lead to official accountability, as well as the disciplinary measures that may follow. The accountability framework was originally released in 2015. An official with the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee said an update was necessary as China has entered a stage of high-quality development featuring accelerated green and low-carbon growth, while the CPC Central Committee has issued a series of new requirements on ecological and environmental protection in recent years. The revised rules broaden the scope of accountability beyond leading Party and government officials to include senior officials at public institutions, development zones and state-owned enterprises. China has pledged to bring carbon dioxide emissions to a peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. The revised document specifies that local officials who fail to effectively advance these efforts will also be held accountable. Meanwhile, the official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee noted that accountability for ecological and environmental damage must be precise and evidence-based. "It should neither dampen officials' enthusiasm for work, nor undermine the credibility of the Party and the government." China has stepped up ecological and environmental protection efforts. During the second round of the central ecological and environmental protection inspections, conducted from May 2020 to June 2022, a total of 3,371 people were held accountable. The third round of such inspections is currently underway. The revised accountability rules also bring them into line with China's Ecological and Environmental Code, which officially took effect on Aug. 15.

item.title: China to revise regulations on housing provident fund management
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-18
BEIJING, Aug. 18 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree publicizing a decision to revise the Regulations on Management of Housing Provident Fund, which will take effect on Sept. 20, 2026. According to the decision, the scope of the fund's withdrawal and use will be expanded. For those withdrawing from the housing provident fund to pay rent, the eligibility threshold requiring rent to exceed a prescribed proportion of a household's wage income will be removed. Housing provident fund savings can be withdrawn for new purposes under the revised regulations, including renovating the homes the contributors live in and paying property management fees for such homes. The decision also states that the channels for the investment and utilization of the housing provident fund will be appropriately broadened, specifying that housing provident fund management centers are allowed to use the funds to purchase policy-oriented financial bonds. To enhance the efficiency of management services, the decision also underscores efforts to simplify the procedures for employees to apply for housing provident fund withdrawals and to shorten the review period for housing provident fund loan applications. The decision, which strengthens risk prevention and control, stipulates that housing provident fund management centers should establish comprehensive, complete and accurate credit records and incorporate them into the national credit information sharing platform. Amid efforts to expand the coverage of the system, the decision clarifies that individual business owners, part-time employees and other people in flexible employment can pay voluntary contributions into the housing provident fund and enjoy policy support in accordance with the regulations.
